 JUDGMENT

This claim petition is filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the respondents, claiming compensation of Rs.6,00,000/- with respect to damages caused to the vehicle in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
The petitioner is the R C owner of Maruti Suzuki Swift car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-NC-2303 and was using the said car for his business and family purpose.

That on 11-01-2024 at about 9-45 am., the friend of the petitioner by name A n i l w a s d r i v i n g t h e a f o r e s a i d M a r u t i S u z u k i S w i f t c a r b e a r i n g Reg.no.KA-05-NC-2303 from Sagar towards Sigandhuru and when they reached near Kooranakoppa bus stand, Kooranakoppa village, Sagara Taluk, Shivamogga, at that time the driver of Innova Crista car bearing Reg.No.KA-50-Z-2315 came from opposite direction ie., from Sigandhuru towards Sagara side in a rash and negligent manner and came to the extreme right side of the road and dashed against the petitioner's car, result of which the petitioner's car was badly damaged.
The vehicle of the petitioner was towed to M/s Mandovi Motors Pvt. Ltd., from the accident spot.

After survey the service station has issued Service Estimation to the tune of Rs.2,23,929/- towards replacing new spare parts, tinkering, painting, lathe work,
labour charges etc. excluding towing charges from the accident spot to the show room.
The vehicle of the petitioner is in the garage till filing petition.
During these period the petitioner could not attend to his business, resulted in loss of earnings.
Though the petitioner's car was repaired but its resale value went down.
3. It is further contended that the jurisdictional police have registered a case against the driver of the offending vehicle in crime No.7/2024 for the offences punishable under Sec.279 of IPC.
The accident was occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
The 1st respondent is the owner and 2nd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

4. The respondent no.1/the RC owner of Innova Crista car bearing Reg.No.KA-50-Z-2315 has filed written statement and submitted that his car was insured with the respondent no.2 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.

He further contended that the alleged accident was due to the Abhishek L vs Lakkanna R on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158800310/
2 negligent act on the part of the driver of the vehicle of the petitioner who without observing the traffic rules and regulations dashed against the vehicle of the respondent no.1 and though the respondent no.1 has made his best effort to avoid the accident by applying break but he could not avoid the accident.

sentences.text: The respondent no.1 has disputed the repairing expenses allegedly incurred by the petitioner.

5. Respondent No.2- the insurer of Innova Crista car bearing Reg.No.KA-50-Z-2315 has filed written statement and contended that the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties and that their insured vehicle was not at all involved in the accident and the petitioner has filed a false case against the driver of their insured vehicle.

As like the respondent no.1, even the respondent no.2 has disputed the genuineness of the bill produced by the petitioner and disputed the repairing bill to the tune of Rs.2,22,926/- incurred by the petitioner.

6. On the basis of rival pleadings following issues have been framed;
1) Whether the petitioner proves that in this accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of driving of offending Innova Crista Car bearing Reg.No.KA-50- Z-2315 and as a result, the Murtuhi Suzuki swift car bearing Reg.no.KA-05- NC-2302 sustained damages?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what extend and from whom ?
3) What Order or Award?
7. In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.18.
The respondents have not adduced any evidence on their behalf.

8. Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and respondents and perused the entire materials placed on record.
9.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;

REASONS 10. Issue No.1 : - In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 11-01-2024 at about 9-45 am., the friend of the petitioner by name Anil was driving the Maruti Suzuki Swift car bearing Reg.no.KA-05-NC- 2303 from Sagar towards Sigandhuru and when they reached near Kooranakoppa bus stand, Kooranakoppa village, Sagara Taluk, Shivamogga, at that time the driver of Innova Crista car bearing Reg.No.KA-50-Z-2315 came from opposite direction ie., from Sigandhuru towards Sagara side in a rash and negligent manner and came to the extreme right side of the road and dashed against the petitioner's car, result of which the petitioner's car was badly Abhishek L vs Lakkanna R on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158800310/
3 damaged.

11. In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1, 2 and Ex.P11 to 17 which are the police records such as F.I.R with complaint, charge sheet,
IMV report, spot mahazar, photograph pertaining to scene of the occurrence, sketch, seizer mahazar, indemnity bond, statement of witnesses etc.,
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Sri Lakkanna R., case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.0007/2024 of Sagar Rural Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279 of IPC.

After completion of investigation, the investigating officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 279 of IPC.
13.

Though the respondent no.1 and 2 in their written statement have disputed the manner of accident stated by the petitioner but if the complaint at Ex.P1 is perused, the complaint came to be filed by the inmate of the offending vehicle by name R Lakkanna.

The inmate of the offending vehicle by lodging the complaint has stated that on the date of accident when they were proceeding towards Bangalore from Sigandhuru, the driver of their vehicle drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and in order to avoid the cow passing on the road, he took his vehicle towards the right side result of which it hit to the vehicle of the petitioner.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by the complainant, case has been registered against the driver of the offending vehicle and after investigation charge sheet was filed against the driver of the offending vehicle.

When the inmate of the offending vehicle being an eye witness himself has lodged the complaint against the driver of the offending vehicle, the court cannot accept the contradictory statement taken by the owner of the offending vehicle in his written statement.

Further if the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, it is not in dispute that at the time of accident the offending vehicle was proceeding from Sigandhuru towards Sagar and the vehicle of the petitioner was proceeding from Sagar towards Sigandhuru .
The spot of accident is towards the right side of Sigandhuru - Sagar road.

It clearly reveals that the driver of the offending vehicle took his vehicle towards the right side of the road and hit to the vehicle of the petitioner which was proceeding on the left side of the road.

Hence, the very complaint lodged by the inmate of the offending vehicle coupled with the spot mahazar and sketch and very fact that respondents have not taken steps to examine the driver of the offending vehicle would clearly proves the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and his caused for the accident.
Hence, without discussing much on this point, above point is answered in the Affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:- The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of damage caused to his vehicle as the impact of the accident and the amount spent by him towards repair of the vehicle.

The petitioner has produced Bills, Invoices, Towing bill dated 11-01-2024 and Insurance policy as per Ex.P.6 to Ex.P8.
15.

The Pw.1 nowhere in his evidence has stated or has not produced any document to let the court know the date on which his damaged vehicle was kept for repair and the date on which he has taken delivery of the vehicle from the service center after its being repaired.

The court can take judicial notice that in the service station they will maintain register in which they will mention the date on which the vehicle was kept for repair and the date on which the vehicle was delivered after its being Abhishek L vs Lakkanna R on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158800310/
4 repaired.
The petitioner has not produced job card.
He has not produced survey report and has not examined the surveyor.
Without there being the survey report and the evidence of surveyor it is hard to accept the invoices produced by the petitioner in its entirety.
The petitioner even has not examined the concerned person from Mandovi Motors Pvt Ltd., from whom the damaged vehicle was repaired.

Without there being any authenticated evidence to prove that the petitioner has incurred repairing expense to the tune of Rs.2,17,191/-, the court cannot accept the said amount as the expenses incurred by the petitioner for the repair of the damage caused from the accident.
If Ex.P6 and Ex.P7 are perused, it can be make out that the vehicle was kept for repair on 13-01-2024 because in the Ex.P7 there is job card date 13-01-2024.
The entire payment towards repairing expenses to the tune of Rs.2,17,191/- was paid on 29-02-2024.
Hence, it can be said that it is after the vehicle was being repaired, the petitioner had paid net amount of Rs.2,17,191/- which includes labour charges.

But this court decline to award sum of Rs.2,17,191/- towards repair charges for the reason that there is no materials placed on record by the petitioner to say that all the aforesaid repairing expenses was towards the damage caused to the vehicle due to the accident in question.

Hence, because of lack of evidence, this court inclines to award compensation under the head repair charges to the tune of Rs.1,00,000/-.
16.
The petitioner has produced repair total amounting to Rs.20,000/- for having hired the vehicle for towing the damaged vehicle from the spot of accident to the service station at Bangalore.

It is true that the petitioner could have hired vehicle from the place where the accident in question has occurred but it does not make any much difference even if vehicle is hired from Bangalore or from the accident place.

Because even if vehicle is hired from the accident place, after towing the vehicle to Mandovi Motors at Bangalore they have to return to accident place only and the distance would be the same even if vehicle is hired from Bangalore or from accident place.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.20,000/- towards towing charges.
17. It is submitted by the petitioner that he is a business man and that because the vehicle was kept for repair he could not use the vehicle for nearly 6 months.
But petitioner has not stated what was the loss incurred by him due to the vehicle was kept for service.
But when the vehicle of the petitioner was in garage for some period, the possibility of petitioner hired some vehicle for his day to day work cannot be ruled out.
Hence, this court inclines to award sum of Rs.15,000/- towards hire charges.
18. Hence, this court considers that the total loss caused to the petitioner due to the damage caused to the vehicle at Rs.1,35,000/-.
Hence, respondent no.2 is liable to compensate the petitioner sum of Rs.1,35,000/- with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly issue no 2 is answered in partly affirmative.
19. Issue No.3:- In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
